Translate an RNA strand, three nucleotides at a time, into the amino acids of its protein, stopping at the first STOP codon.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/protein-translation) (MIT). Listed under [Encoding & Ciphers](/examples/?subject=encoding-and-ciphers).

```nomi-run
// FILE: protein_translation.nomi
//# Translates an RNA strand, three nucleotides at a time, into the amino
//# acids of its protein.

/// The amino acids the exercise's codons stand for.
pub enum AminoAcid {
    Methionine
    Phenylalanine
    Leucine
    Serine
    Tyrosine
    Cysteine
    Tryptophan
}

/// Why a strand does not translate.
pub enum Error {
    /// A codon before the first STOP that stands for nothing, given as it
    /// appears in the strand: three letters, or fewer at the strand's end.
    InvalidCodon String
}

/// The amino acids `strand`'s codons stand for, up to its first STOP codon.
/// Whatever follows a STOP is not read.
pub fn proteins(strand: String) -> Result<List<AminoAcid>, Error> {
    strand
    |> Iter.chunks(3)
    |> Iter.map(String.join)
    |> Iter.map(translate)
    |> Iter.take_while(&(&1 != Ok(None)))
    |> Result.collect()
    |> Result.map(Maybe.values)
}

/// The amino acid `codon` stands for, `None` for a STOP codon.
fn translate(codon: String) -> Result<Maybe<AminoAcid>, Error> {
    case codon {
        "AUG" -> Ok(Some(.Methionine))
        "UUU" or "UUC" -> Ok(Some(.Phenylalanine))
        "UUA" or "UUG" -> Ok(Some(.Leucine))
        "UCU" or "UCC" or "UCA" or "UCG" -> Ok(Some(.Serine))
        "UAU" or "UAC" -> Ok(Some(.Tyrosine))
        "UGU" or "UGC" -> Ok(Some(.Cysteine))
        "UGG" -> Ok(Some(.Tryptophan))
        "UAA" or "UAG" or "UGA" -> Ok(None)
        _ -> Err(.InvalidCodon(codon))
    }
}

// FILE: protein_translation_test.nomi
import {
    protein_translation
    protein_translation.{AminoAcid, Error}
}

test "proteins" {
    cases = [
        #("Empty RNA sequence results in no proteins", "", []),
        #("Methionine RNA sequence", "AUG", [AminoAcid.Methionine]),
        #("Phenylalanine RNA sequence 1", "UUU", [.Phenylalanine]),
        #("Phenylalanine RNA sequence 2", "UUC", [.Phenylalanine]),
        #("Leucine RNA sequence 1", "UUA", [.Leucine]),
        #("Leucine RNA sequence 2", "UUG", [.Leucine]),
        #("Serine RNA sequence 1", "UCU", [.Serine]),
        #("Serine RNA sequence 2", "UCC", [.Serine]),
        #("Serine RNA sequence 3", "UCA", [.Serine]),
        #("Serine RNA sequence 4", "UCG", [.Serine]),
        #("Tyrosine RNA sequence 1", "UAU", [.Tyrosine]),
        #("Tyrosine RNA sequence 2", "UAC", [.Tyrosine]),
        #("Cysteine RNA sequence 1", "UGU", [.Cysteine]),
        #("Cysteine RNA sequence 2", "UGC", [.Cysteine]),
        #("Tryptophan RNA sequence", "UGG", [.Tryptophan]),
        #("STOP codon RNA sequence 1", "UAA", []),
        #("STOP codon RNA sequence 2", "UAG", []),
        #("STOP codon RNA sequence 3", "UGA", []),
        #(
            "Sequence of two protein codons translates into proteins",
            "UUUUUU",
            [.Phenylalanine, .Phenylalanine],
        ),
        #(
            "Sequence of two different protein codons translates into proteins",
            "UUAUUG",
            [.Leucine, .Leucine],
        ),
        #(
            "Translate RNA strand into correct protein list",
            "AUGUUUUGG",
            [.Methionine, .Phenylalanine, .Tryptophan],
        ),
        #("Translation stops if STOP codon at beginning of sequence", "UAGUGG", []),
        #("Translation stops if STOP codon at end of two-codon sequence", "UGGUAG", [.Tryptophan]),
        #(
            "Translation stops if STOP codon at end of three-codon sequence",
            "AUGUUUUAA",
            [.Methionine, .Phenylalanine],
        ),
        #(
            "Translation stops if STOP codon in middle of three-codon sequence",
            "UGGUAGUGG",
            [.Tryptophan],
        ),
        #(
            "Translation stops if STOP codon in middle of six-codon sequence",
            "UGGUGUUAUUAAUGGUUU",
            [.Tryptophan, .Cysteine, .Tyrosine],
        ),
        #(
            "Sequence of two non-STOP codons does not translate to a STOP codon",
            "AUGAUG",
            [.Methionine, .Methionine],
        ),
        #(
            "Incomplete RNA sequence can translate if valid until a STOP codon",
            "UUCUUCUAAUGGU",
            [.Phenylalanine, .Phenylalanine],
        ),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, strand, expected), description {
        assert protein_translation.proteins(strand) == Ok(expected)
    }
}

test "invalid codons" {
    cases = [
        #(
            "Unknown amino acids, not part of a codon, can't translate",
            "XYZ",
            Error.InvalidCodon("XYZ"),
        ),
        #("Incomplete RNA sequence can't translate", "AUGU", .InvalidCodon("U")),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, strand, expected), description {
        assert protein_translation.proteins(strand) == Err(expected)
    }
}
```

## How it's written

- Amino acids are an `AminoAcid` enum, not the canonical strings.
- The error is `Error.InvalidCodon(String)`, carrying the codon that did not translate: `"XYZ"`, or the short tail `"U"` of `"AUGU"`. The canonical data gives only the message "Invalid codon".
- `proteins` is one pipeline: `Iter.chunks(3)` cuts the codons, `translate` reads each as `Result<Maybe<AminoAcid>, Error>` with `Ok(None)` for STOP, `Iter.take_while` stops at the first STOP, `Result.collect` keeps the first error, and `Maybe.values` unwraps the amino acids. Because `take_while` is lazy, nothing after a STOP is read, which is why `"UUCUUCUAAUGGU"` translates despite its short tail.
- STOP is `None` rather than a variant of a private `Codon` enum. A `Codon` enum names it better, but its `Stop` would have to be filtered out again after `take_while`, the same as `None` is.
- `Iter.map(String.join)` passes the function itself: where a function of one parameter is expected, `String.join` takes its default separator.
- "Non-existing codon can't translate" (`"AAA"`) is left out: "Unknown amino acids, not part of a codon, can't translate" reimplements it.
- The success table has no type annotation. Its first row's expected list is `[]`, and its second row writes `AminoAcid.Methionine` qualified, so the bare variants in later rows take `AminoAcid` from it.
